In 1969, Apollo 11 landed on the Moon, and Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on its surface.
In 1903, the Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. It lasted 12 seconds.
In 1928, Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin after noticing that mold had stopped bacteria growing in a dish he'd left out.
Around 1440, Johannes Gutenberg developed his printing press, and books became something ordinary people could own.
In 1876, Alexander Graham Bell made the first telephone call, to his assistant Thomas Watson in the next room.
In 1955, Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, sparking the Montgomery bus boycott.
In 1989, the Berlin Wall came down after dividing the city for 28 years.
In 1991, Tim Berners-Lee put the first website online.
In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick, building on Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images, described the double-helix structure of DNA.
In 1962, John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth.
In 1981, the first Space Shuttle, Columbia, launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
In 1886, Vicente Martinez Ybor started making cigars in Tampa, and Ybor City grew into the cigar capital of the world.
In 1891, the Tampa Bay Hotel opened. Today its silver minarets top the University of Tampa's Plant Hall.
In 1927, Charles Lindbergh flew solo and nonstop from New York to Paris in about 33 and a half hours.
In 1932, Amelia Earhart became the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.
In 1879, Thomas Edison tested a light bulb that lasted long enough to be practical.
In 1990, the Hubble Space Telescope launched into orbit.
In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue computer beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a match.
In 2007, Apple introduced the first iPhone.
In 1964, the Civil Rights Act was signed into law in the United States.
In 1920, the 19th Amendment was ratified, giving American women the right to vote.
In 1863, the London Underground opened as the world's first underground railway.
In 1886, the Statue of Liberty was dedicated in New York Harbor.
In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers known to reach the top of Mount Everest.
In 1914, the Panama Canal opened, linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
In 1936, Jesse Owens won four gold medals at the Berlin Olympics.
In 1947, Jackie Robinson broke Major League Baseball's color barrier with the Brooklyn Dodgers.
In 1958, NASA was created.
In 1976, Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple.
In 1998, Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google.
In 1977, Voyager 1 launched. It's now the farthest human-made object from Earth.
In 1513, Juan Ponce de León reached Florida and named it La Florida.
In 1845, Florida became the 27th state.
